document.abstract: Three methods of reducing the final wash requirement in the Eastman Color Print process are reviewed: (1) higher final wash temperatures; (2) hypo clearing baths; and (3) oxidation of thiosulfate to sulfate. A sulfite clearing bath at pH 5.8 followed by a short final wash is a practical and effective technique of hypo removal. Normal dye stability can be expected as long as proper film emulsion pH (range 5.0 to 6.0) and residual hypo (less than 4/μg/cm2) levels are maintained.
